### Mayoral terms and term limits in New York City since 1834
Mayors John T. Hoffman (1866–1868, elected Governor 1868), William Havemeyer (1845–1846, 1848–1849, and 1873–1874), William Jay Gaynor (1910–1913), John Francis Hylan (1918–1925), Jimmy Walker (1926–1932), and [William O'Dwyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_O'Dwyer "William O'Dwyer") (1946–1950) failed to complete the final terms to which they were elected. The uncompleted mayoral terms of Hoffman, Walker, and O'Dwyer were added to the other offices elected in (respectively) 1868, 1932, and 1950. Those three elections are listed as "special" in the table below because they occurred before the next regularly scheduled _mayoral_ election; the "regular" mayoral elections of 1874 and 1913, on the other hand, were held on the same day that they would have happened had the mayoralty not become vacant.

### Mayoral terms and term limits in New York City since 1834
1.   Mayor Havemeyer was a Democrat who ran as a Republican against the Democratic Tweed Ring in 1872.  
2.   Acting Mayors Coman, Vance, Kline and Collins did not seek election as mayor.  
3.   Acting Mayors McKee and Impellitteri were Democrats who lost the Democratic primary to succeed themselves, but still ran in the general election as independents.  
4.   Elected Mayor Oakey Hall won re-election, while Mayor Wickham did not seek it. Mayors Mitchel and O'Brien lost attempts at re-election, while Mayor Impellitteri did not run for a full term in the 1953 regular general election after losing the Democratic primary.
Brooklyn elected a mayor from 1834 until its consolidation into the City of Greater New York in 1898, whose own second mayor, Seth Low, had been mayor of Brooklyn from 1881 to 1885. Since 1898, Brooklyn has, in place of a separate mayor, elected a borough president.
Long Island City, now a neighborhood within the borough of Queens, was incorporated as a city on May 4, 1870 and was consolidated into the present City of Greater New York on January 1, 1898, along with the city of Brooklyn and several other municipalities in the counties of Queens and Richmond.

### Mayoral terms and term limits in New York City since 1834
1.   ↑Matthias Nicoll's second non-consecutive term as mayor was erroneously excluded from the official numbering of mayors due to the contemporary records of his second term being misplaced, leading to a misnumbering of every subsequent mayor. The error was first noted as early as 1935, and was later officially corrected upon the inauguration of Zohran Mamdani in 2026.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-4)  
2.   ↑Peter Delanoy was the first and only popularly-elected mayor of New York City until 1834. The office of mayor was resumed to be governor-appointed in the wake of [Leisler's Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leisler's_Rebellion "Leisler's Rebellion").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-6)  
3.   ↑Charles Lodwick was excluded from the list of mayors of New York City until the error was officially corrected in 1937.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-:0-8)  
4.   Jump up to: 12345Died in office  
5.   Jump up to: 12345Resigned from office  
6.   ↑As a result of a conflict between the Republican-dominated New York State Legislature and the Tammany Hall political machine, Fernando Wood's second consecutive term as mayor was shortened by a year through a vote passed by both chambers of the legislature to revise the New York City Charter. A mayoral election for a standard-length term was held later that year, resulting in the incumbent Wood's loss to independent candidate Daniel F. Tiemann.  

### Mayoral terms and term limits in New York City since 1834
7.   ↑Thomas Coman became acting mayor upon the resignation of John T. Hoffman.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-14)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-15)  
8.   ↑Common Council president John Cochrane served as acting mayor when A. Oakey Hall temporarily stepped down from office in January 1872.  
9.   ↑Samuel B. H. Vance became acting mayor upon the death of William Frederick Havemeyer.  
10.   ↑William Lafayette Strong served an additional year in office because New York City mayoral elections were changed to be held in odd-numbered years due to the impending consolidation of the city.  
11.   ↑City Council presidentRandolph Gugghenheimer served as acting mayor multiple times throughout the mayoralty of Robert Anderson Van Wyck whenever Van Wyck was not present in the city.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-20)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-21)  
12.   ↑Ardolph L. Kline became acting mayor upon the death of William Jay Gaynor  
13.   ↑William T. Collins became acting mayor upon the resignation of John Francis Hylan, one day prior to the inauguration of Jimmy Walker.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-26)  
14.   ↑Joseph V. McKee became acting mayor upon the resignation of Jimmy Walker.  
15.   ↑Vincent R. Impellitteri became acting mayor upon the resignation of William O'Dwyer on August 31, 1950, and was then elected mayor in a special election held on November 7. He was inaugurated a week later on November 14.  

### Mayoral terms and term limits in New York City since 1834
16.   ↑John Lindsay left the Republican Party in favor of the Democratic Party in 1971 in preparation for his unsuccessful campaign for the Democratic nomination for U.S. president in the following year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-31)  
17.   ↑Michael Bloomberg was a lifelong member of the Democratic Party before registering as a Republican in 2001 and running for mayor. He left the Republican Party in 2007 and ran as an independent candidate in the 2009 mayoral election, later registering as a Democrat again in 2018 in preparation for his unsuccessful campaign for the Democratic nomination for U.S. president in 2020.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_New_York_City#cite_note-33)  
18.   ↑George H. Hunter served as acting mayor from September 1873 to April 1874 while Henry S. DeBevoise temporarily stepped down from office.
